blocks.text: Half-day city tour of Santiago: the historic centre with the Plaza de Armas, the Post Office, the City Hall, La Moneda Palace and Santa Lucía Hill, then the modern residential and commercial districts in the east of the city. Continue to the Maipo Valley, known for its vineyards beneath the Andes, to learn about grape growing and winemaking and taste its wines. Transfer to the airport for your flight home.

blocks.text:
## Journey highlights

The first days in Brazil focus on Rio's main panoramic views and the Iguazu Falls. In Rio, you will visit Christ the Redeemer and Sugar Loaf. In Foz do Iguaçu, the programme includes the Brazilian side of the falls, Macuco Safari and the Bird Park, followed the next day by the Argentine side.

The Argentine section begins in Buenos Aires, with a city tour, historic neighbourhoods, a tango show and dinner. The route then heads to Patagonia, El Calafate and the Perito Moreno Glacier.

After Argentina, the journey continues in Chile. Puerto Natales serves as the base for visiting Torres del Paine, followed by Santiago and the Atacama Desert, with stargazing, the Valley of the Moon and high-altitude lagoons.

The final day returns to Santiago and the Maipo Valley, combining a city tour with a vineyard visit and wine tasting.

## Three countries in one itinerary

The Brazilian section offers a striking contrast between a large city and tropical nature. Rio is surrounded by green hills, bays and the ocean. Copacabana reveals the city's everyday beach life, while Corcovado and Sugar Loaf let you see Rio from above, from different perspectives. Iguazu continues the nature theme in a different setting: subtropical rainforest and a vast system of cascades replace the ocean.

In Foz do Iguaçu, the journey offers several ways to experience the region. Panoramic walkways and viewpoints come first, followed by Macuco Safari, travelling along the river and approaching the falls. The Bird Park introduces tropical species, including toucans, parrots and flamingos. The next day, the Argentine side brings you closer to the water and offers different views of individual cascades.

Buenos Aires replaces natural scenery with a city programme: architecture, historic squares, San Telmo, tango culture, Argentine steaks and Malbec. An evening tango show follows the daytime tour.

The scenery then changes dramatically again. Santa Cruz Province welcomes you with rugged Patagonian landscapes, glaciers and vast open spaces. The main highlight is Perito Moreno in Los Glaciares National Park. You can observe its movement from the viewpoints, while large blocks of ice break off with a thunderous roar.

Puerto Natales provides the gateway to Chilean Patagonia. The town itself is small, with colourful houses and markets, and is a convenient starting point for Torres del Paine. The park brings together granite peaks, glacial lakes, forests, grassy plains and glaciers. Here you will see Lago Pehoé, Lago Grey and Grey Glacier; the region is home to guanacos, foxes, pumas, condors and other birds.

The Atacama offers another kind of landscape. The high, dry desert, minimal light pollution and clear skies make the area suitable for astronomical observation. The programme includes exploring the night sky through telescopes and visiting Valle de la Luna, with its salt formations, dunes and rocks.

The next day, you will head higher still, to lagoons more than 4,000 m above sea level. Their vivid waters contrast with the dry ground and snow-capped volcanoes. Licancabur rises above the landscape.

The itinerary ends with urban sights and local flavours. Santiago offers a historic centre and modern districts, while the Maipo Valley introduces vineyards and local winemaking techniques. Wine tasting concludes the journey before your airport transfer.

## Travel arrangements and format

The itinerary involves several domestic flights. They link Rio with Foz do Iguaçu, Iguazu with Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires with El Calafate, the south of the continent with Santiago, and Santiago with the Atacama. Domestic flights are excluded from the base price and cost from USD 1,500 per person.

Transfers are included. On different days, you will be met by a driver, a driver and guide, or an Ada Tours representative. Sightseeing days are followed by returns to hotels or direct transfers to airports.

The excursion format varies by region. Major cities focus on sightseeing routes and cultural landmarks. At Iguazu, a boat excursion complements the walking paths. In Patagonia, the main sights are viewed from observation platforms and nature trails. In the Atacama, some activities take place in the evening and at night because of the astronomy programme.

Hotel breakfasts and dinner at the tango show in Buenos Aires are included. Meals not specified in the programme are paid for separately.

Guiding arrangements also vary throughout the journey: some places have a guide and driver, others provide only a driver for transfers, and some nature excursions are led by specialist local guides.

## Contrasting natural landscapes

Rio combines the ocean, urban neighbourhoods and Tijuca Forest. Iguazu reveals humid subtropical rainforest, where the constant sound of water, mist from the cascades and abundant birds create a very different environment.

El Calafate takes the journey into cold Patagonia. Ice becomes the main focus here, with Lago Argentino, the mountains and Perito Moreno Glacier defining the scale of the landscape. Further on, Torres del Paine adds grassy plains, granite massifs, glacial lakes and wildlife.

The Atacama represents the opposite kind of environment: a dry high-altitude desert, salt formations, dunes and clear night skies. The high-altitude lagoons lie above 4,000 m, making the conditions on this day noticeably different from the tropical beginning of the journey.
